facts.raw_span: 2 months of progressive proximal muscle weakness
difficulty combing her hair and rising from a chair
morning stiffness of both small hand joints lasting about 30 minutes
dysphagia for solids and liquids
without fever or weight loss
symmetric muscle strength of 4/5 in the upper limbs and 3/5 in the lower limbs
brisk reflexes more pronounced on the left
leukopenia (WBC 2.96 × 10^3/µL)
microcytic anemia (hemoglobin 10.4 g/dL)
elevated C-reactive protein (18.8 mg/L) and erythrocyte sedimentation rate (109.2 mm/hr)
bilateral sacroiliitis
bilateral thigh intramuscular edema with enhancement

concepts.why: Progressive proximal muscle weakness, morning stiffness, and elevated inflammatory markers support this diagnosis.
Suppressed TSH, elevated free T4, and anti-thyroglobulin antibodies indicate thyroiditis.
Bilateral sacroiliitis on MRI supports this diagnosis.
Dysphagia and bilateral thigh intramuscular edema with enhancement suggest this diagnosis.
Microcytic anemia and elevated anti-thyroglobulin antibodies support this diagnosis.
Morning stiffness and elevated inflammatory markers suggest this diagnosis.
Suppressed TSH and elevated free T4 indicate thyroid dysfunction, which can be associated with orbitopathy.
Progressive proximal muscle weakness and elevated inflammatory markers support this diagnosis.

rationales.F01: Progressive proximal muscle weakness is a hallmark of Juvenile Dermatomyositis and Inflammatory Myopathy.
rationales.F06: Symmetric muscle strength reduction is characteristic of Juvenile Dermatomyositis and Inflammatory Myopathy.
rationales.F10: Elevated C-reactive protein and erythrocyte sedimentation rate indicate inflammation, which is common in Juvenile Dermatomyositis, Sacroiliitis, and Rheumatoid Arthritis.
rationales.F11: Bilateral sacroiliitis is a key feature of Sacroiliitis and can be associated with other autoimmune conditions.

frontier_selector.rationale: Progressive proximal muscle weakness, morning stiffness, and specific joint involvement support Juvenile Dermatomyositis, with Inflammatory Myopathy as a close runner-up due to similar muscle weakness symptoms.
